subject: Commit restructure & termination mechanics — BlueWave
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@bluewavehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: BlueWave Procurement <procurement@bluewavehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — multi-year commit structure and exit mechanics

Karthik,

Thanks again for walking us through Redwood's offering yesterday. BlueWave is interested in a multi-year purchase but we need clarity on a few commercial mechanics before we proceed to internal procurement:

- We prefer an "annualized upfront" approach where each year is prepaid up-front but with a consolidated three-year master commitment. That said, we expect step-up ramp in consumption across years (Q1 small pilot -> Q3 production).
- Critical: early termination/refund mechanics if we choose to exit an individual year or the whole agreement — how do you handle unconsumed prepay and the discounted rate applied for multi-year?
- Co-terming: if we expand to other BU's, can you co-term or will we lose favorable pricing?
- Example: if we prepay $600k for year 1 (discounted), then usage only consumes $380k before termination, what refund do we see and what fees apply?

Attached is the RFP and a high-level usage profile. Can you share a clear matrix (numbers) and a proposed termination clause (both for partial-year exits and full early termination) so we can route to procurement/legal?

Looking forward — happy to set a short call next week.

Sara Patel
Head of Data Products
BlueWave Health
Attachments: 2025-09-10_BlueWave_RFP.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@bluewavehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — multi-year commit structure and exit mechanics

Sara — thanks for the clear note and the RFP. We can make the economics predictable while preserving ramp flexibility. High-level proposal below; I'll attach a worked matrix for your team and loop in Legal for precise contract language.

Key points:
- Structure: three-year master with annual prepay invoices (you invoice for Year 1, Year 2, Year 3 on annual cadence) but with an annualized blended discount for committing multi-year. This avoids accounting headaches while keeping the discount tied to total commitment.
- Refund / early termination (commercial intent): refundable_amount = unamortized_prepaid_value - earned_usage_amount - discount_recapture.
  - "Unamortized prepaid value" = portion of the year remaining on an amortization schedule (monthly).
  - "Earned usage" = actual consumption valued at the effective (post-discount) per-token/unit rate; this prevents double-crediting.
  - "Discount recapture" = pro-rated clawback tied to years remaining (higher in year 1, tapering thereafter).
- Practical early-exit fee: rather than an open negotiation, propose a capped exit fee equal to 20% of the remaining committed value if termination occurs within 12 months of the invoice; 10% in months 13-24; 0% afterward. This gives both predictability and incentive to continue.
- Co-terming: we can co-term new BU additions but only if added within 90 days of the next anniversary; pricing additive usage at the same blended rate but with a separate ramp credit to smooth step-changes. Co-terming requires a short SOW to scope BU-specific volumes.

I'm attaching a term matrix (RW-BH-347_term_matrix.xlsx) with three example scenarios including the $600k -> $380k use case. Lauren, can you review the termination wording below and propose redlines?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RW-BH-347_term_matrix.xlsx

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Sara Patel <sara.patel@bluewavehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — multi-year commit structure and exit mechanics (contract redline suggestions)

Karthik / Sara — I reviewed the commercial approach and drafted a clean, legally-sound termination clause for your sample scenarios. High-level changes I recommend:

1) Refund calculation (replace formula language with explicit steps):
   - Determine remaining prepaid balance at termination date.
   - Subtract actual consumption valued at the blended per-unit rate agreed in Appendix A.
   - Subtract any "Discount Clawback" equal to the pro-rated portion of multi-year discount (calculated on a straight-line basis across the full contracted term).
   - Apply any fixed termination fee (20%/10%/0% ladder) if termination occurs within the defined windows.

2) Notice & timeline: require 90 days written notice for a partial-year exit or reallocation of committed units to alternate BUs. Refunds paid within 60 days after final usage reconciliation.

3) Co-terming / BU additions: require a signed SOW for each BU addition; if co-terming is requested at the time of SOW, parties will agree an amortization schedule for any ramp credits.

4) Audit & reconciliation: Redwood retains right to audit usage up to 12 months after termination to validate earned usage.

I've attached a redline (RW-BH-347_redline.docx) with exact language for Appendix B (Termination & Refunds) and Appendix C (Co-terming & Ramp Credits). The redline preserves a customer-friendly refund while protecting Redwood from large unearned discounts being refunded in full.

Happy to jump on a 20-minute call to walk through this.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
Attachments: RW-BH-347_redline.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial ask — multi-year commit structure and exit mechanics

Sara — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per your ask, attached is the worked example (RW-BH-347_term_matrix.xlsx) showing three scenarios:

A) Early exit in month 8 of Year 1: shows unamortized prepay, earned usage at blended rate, 20% early-exit fee, and net refund.
B) Partial reallocation at month 14 (Year 2): demonstrates SOW-triggered co-term, amortization transfer and a small ramp smoothing credit.
C) Full termination in month 30: minimal recapture and pro-rated refund.

Next steps: if these outputs look good to you, we can have your procurement sign the attached term exhibit and I'll send a DocuSign envelope for the master order form + Appendix B/C. If you prefer, we can add an escrow option for disputed refunds — we can discuss tradeoffs.

Proposed times for a final align call this week: Thu 10/2 4pm PT or Fri 10/3 11am PT.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
